title: MiniMax H3, node by node, with sound in the same latent

questions.q: How do VAEDecode and VAEDecodeAudio both read from one sampler output?
options: The latent is nested: VAEDecode takes the first stream and VAEDecodeAudio takes the last
The sampler has two output sockets, one for each
The audio is hidden in the alpha channel
VAEDecode makes both and VAEDecodeAudio copies it
questions.answer: The latent is nested: VAEDecode takes the first stream and VAEDecodeAudio takes the last
questions.why: VAEDecode uses latent.unbind()[0] when the latent is nested, and vae_decode_audio uses unbind()[-1].

questions.q: Where does the number 5/3 come from?
options: 40 audio latent frames a second divided by 24 video frames a second
5 video latent frames per 3 cycles
The audio shift divided by the video shift
The stereo channel count
questions.answer: 40 audio latent frames a second divided by 24 video frames a second
questions.why: FRAME_RESCALE puts both streams on one clock: 32000 Hz over a hop of 800 is 40 a second, and 40 / 24 = 5/3.

questions.q: The sampler only follows one schedule. How can audio use a different shift?
options: The audio stream is carried scaled by the ratio of shifts, and the model converts the noise level with time_shift_sigma
Audio is sampled in a second run afterwards
The audio shift is ignored
The audio latent gets no noise
questions.answer: The audio stream is carried scaled by the ratio of shifts, and the model converts the noise level with time_shift_sigma
questions.why: ModelSamplingAV's audio_scale is shift / audio_shift, 4 by default, and the model maps the video sigma to the audio sigma.

questions.q: Decoding H3 runs short of memory, so you swap in VAEDecodeTiled with small tiles. What changes?
options: Nothing much: H3's decode_tiled ignores the tile settings and calls decode, which already chunks internally
Memory falls with the tile size, as on other VAEs
The audio is decoded in tiles too
The sampler restarts with fewer tokens
questions.answer: Nothing much: H3's decode_tiled ignores the tile settings and calls decode, which already chunks internally
questions.why: handles_tiling is true for this VAE and decode_tiled(z, **kwargs) just returns decode(z). The chunks are built in.

questions.q: Someone changed the graph's seconds value from 5 to 30. What should you do on a first run?
options: Set it near 5: 30 s is 736 frames, past the tooltip's trained range of about 124 to 362
Leave it: the model handles any length equally
Set it to 124, since it counts frames
Leave it, and lower the steps
questions.answer: Set it near 5: 30 s is 736 frames, past the tooltip's trained range of about 124 to 362
questions.why: The PrimitiveFloat holds seconds. The tooltip on the node says longer than about 362 frames is untested, and tokens grow with length.

questions.q: How much of the token count does audio add at 5 seconds and 1344 x 768?
options: About 1.1%
About half
About a quarter
It adds no tokens
questions.why: The lab prints 414 audio tokens against 37,296 video tokens.
